'''Ashwin Rod Gover'''<ref>{{Cite web |title=A. Rod Gover |url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/rod-gover |access-date=30 September 2016 |website=Institute for Advanced Study}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://profiles.auckland.ac.nz/r-gover|title=Professor Rod Gover |website=University of Auckland |access-date=4 February 2023}}</ref> is a New Zealand mathematician and a Fellow of the [[Royal Society of New Zealand]]. He is currently employed as a Professor of [[Pure Mathematics]] at the [[University of Auckland]] in New Zealand.<ref name=":0" />

== Education and career ==
Gover received his secondary education at [[Tauranga Boys' College]], where he was Head Boy and Dux. He earned a Bachelor of Science with Honours and Master of Science in physics at [[University of Canterbury|Canterbury University]] and a Doctor of Philosophy (DPhil) in Mathematics in 1989 at [[University of Oxford|Oxford]]. He joined the University of Auckland as a lecturer in 1999, before being promoted to Senior Lecturer in 2001, Associate Professor in 2005, and Professor in 2008.<ref>{{Cite news |url=http://www.pressreader.com/new-zealand/east-and-bays-courier/20080716/281621006106006 |title=Kudos for Maths expert |date=16 July 2008 |newspaper=[[East & Bays Courier]] |via=PressReader |access-date=30 September 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161001215644/http://www.pressreader.com/new-zealand/east-and-bays-courier/20080716/281621006106006|archive-date=1 October 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> He is an elected Fellow of the [[New Zealand Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Becoming a Fellow of the NZMS |url=https://nzmathsoc.org.nz/about-the-nzms/becoming-a-fellow-of-the-nzms/ |access-date=2025-08-30 |website=New Zealand Mathematical Society |language=en-NZ}}</ref>

== Research areas ==
His current main research areas are
* [[Differential geometry]] and its relationship to representation theory
* Applications to analysis on manifolds, PDE theory and Mathematical Physics
* Conformal, CR and related structures
He has published work on a range of topics including integral transforms and their applications to representation theory and quantum groups. His main area of specialisation is the class of parabolic differential geometries. Tractor calculus is important for treating geometries in this class, and a current theme of his work is the further development of this calculus, its relationship to other geometric constructions and tools, as well as its applications to the construction and understanding of local and global geometric invariants and natural differential equations.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.math.auckland.ac.nz/wiki/Rod_Gover_-_Research|title=Rod Gover – Research – MathsDept |website=University of Auckland |access-date=30 September 2016}}</ref> A list of his publications can be found [https://www.math.auckland.ac.nz/wiki/Rod_Gover_-_Publications here].
